newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish institute sees large rapeseed/barley damage.
newsitem.headline: Polish institute sees large rapeseed/barley damage.

text.p: Poland's Institute of Meteorology and Water Management (IMGW) confirmed Agriculture Ministry forecasts that winter rapeseed and barley losses this year will likely be larger than in 1996, an IMGW official said.
"Our preliminary data suggest that winter crop losses in rapeseed and barley will be larger than last year," IMGW specialist Anna Strzelczak told Reuters on Tuesday.

Earlier, preliminary Agriculture Ministry figures showed that 46 percent of rapeseed and 41 percent of barley crops did not survive the winter, while eight percent of wheat and two percent of rye were destroyed.

Last year 61 percent of the rapeseed crop survived the winter, while 81 percent of barley, 89 percent of wheat and 90 of rye successfully sprouted in 1996, according to Central Statistical Office (GUS) data.
GUS is due to release official damage figures for the 1996/97 winter early next month.

Strzelczak said weather conditions were varied during the March 11-20 period with lower temparatures in the later stages of the period stopping field work and freezing the top layers of soil in many regions.
But she said the recent cold spell would not have a significant effect on crops unless it was sustained into later March and early April.
Strzelczak added that winter wheat and rye sustained some losses over the winter but that they were not nearly as large as those in barley crops.
The IMGW does not give winter crop survival percentages.
